pNone_chapter_1: In a sun-drenched second-floor drawing room in old Calcutta, Byomkesh Bakshi sits in a wooden armchair, leaning back with a thoughtful expression while holding a folded newspaper. Beside him, Ajit Bandyopadhyay sits at a small tea table, looking toward his friend with an inquisitive gaze. Bright morning light streams through a large open window, revealing a distant view of sparrows and pigeons soaring over the bustling city skyline of Harrison Road. Both men are dressed in traditional white pleated dhoti-kurtas, and the room is filled with a calm, scholarly atmosphere marked by wooden bookshelves and the soft glow of a February morning.
